name: Dying To Self
overview: Scripture calls believers to a radical surrender of self, exemplified by taking up the cross daily and following Christ, as Jesus teaches in Matthew 10:38 and Luke 9:23. This dying to self involves a deliberate denial of personal desires and ambitions, recognizing that clinging to life apart from Christ ultimately leads to loss, while losing one's life for Christ and the gospel results in true salvation (Mark 8:35). The metaphor of the grain of wheat in John 12:24 underscores the necessity of death to self for fruitful spiritual life. Romans 6 further emphasizes this transformation by instructing believers to consider themselves dead to sin but alive to God through Jesus Christ, rejecting any notion of continuing in sin under grace.
